[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

> **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.

The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.

Install the skill:

```bash filename="Terminal"
npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
```

Then give the agent this prompt:

Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.

I made the change using the pattern Next 16.4's docs describe for this. It builds, but on this app the related products still show up in the default prefetch, so the first goal isn't met yet.

What I changed:
- `next.config.ts`: turned on `partialPrefetching: true`. Now a default `<Link>` prefetches one shared "App Shell" per route (the page without the parts marked to wait).
- `app/product/page.tsx`: moved the related products into a `RelatedProducts` component inside `<Suspense fallback="Loading related products...">`. It calls `await prefetch()` from `next/cache` before `getRelatedProducts()`. That call is meant to keep the list out of the shared App Shell, while a link with `prefetch={true}` or a real navigation still loads it. `getRelatedProducts` keeps its `'use cache'` and hourly cache setting.
- `app/page.tsx`: the featured link is now `<Link href="/product" prefetch={true}>`, so it asks for the related products before the click.

Checks:
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`: exit 0.
- `npx next build`: exit 0, `/product` is static (revalidate 1h, expire 1d).
- With `next start`, I sent the same prefetch request a default link makes (headers `RSC: 1`, `Next-Router-Prefetch: 1`, `Next-Router-Segment-Prefetch: /product/__PAGE__`). It returned 200 from the static cache, and the response includes the Suspense fallback plus the resolved list ("Compact Widget", "Widget Carry Case").

Why: `/product` has no request-time data, so it is built entirely ahead of time, and in that build nothing is held back. The Next source code for `prefetch()` says so directly: content below it "is excluded from the shell, but it's deliberately included in the static output (and thus in static prefetches)". I didn't test in a browser whether the client throws that data away for a default link. So either way, the featured link will have the related products ready.

To actually keep them out of default prefetches while that link still gets them, you need to pick one of these:
1. Leave it as is and accept that on a fully static route the list comes with the free, CDN-served static prefetch.
2. Make the route render per request by reading something like `cookies()` or `headers()` in the page. `prefetch()` then does hold the list back from the shell, but default prefetches are no longer served as static files.
3. Use `navigation()` instead of `prefetch()`. That keeps the list out of every prefetch, but it also won't be ready from the featured link; it will load after the click.

I restored the `tsconfig.json` edits `next build` made and deleted the build files it created (`.next`, `next-env.d.ts`, `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`). Your existing changes to `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are untouched.
